edges.reason: A unit fraction names one of the equal parts of a whole; unequal pieces do not represent equal unit fractions.
The numerator counts how many copies of the unit fraction are combined.
A number line gives fractions positions and shows their order and distance from zero.
A mixed number combines complete wholes with a remaining fractional part.
Writing whole units as fractions explains why a mixed number and an improper fraction can name the same quantity.
Equivalent fractions let both quantities be measured in equal-sized parts before comparing their numerators.
A common denominator rewrites both addends in equal-sized parts so their numerators can be added.
A common denominator expresses both quantities using the same unit fraction before subtraction.
Fractions with a common denominator count the same-sized parts, so adding combines those counts.
Subtracting removes some copies of the same unit fraction.
Separating each mixed number into whole and fractional parts gives quantities that can be added in matching units.
Understanding the whole and fractional parts allows one whole to be regrouped as fractional parts when needed.
The fraction multiplication rule applies after the mixed number is converted to an improper fraction.
Converting mixed numbers to improper fractions makes their product accessible using fraction multiplication.
After conversion to improper fractions, multiply the numerators and denominators using the fraction product rule.
A mixed number can be rewritten as an improper fraction before interpreting and calculating the quotient.
After converting mixed numbers, division uses the same quotient reasoning as dividing one fraction by another.
Interpreting a fraction as a quotient helps explain fraction division as asking how many groups of the divisor fit.
Multiplying by a reciprocal undoes multiplication by a nonzero fraction, explaining the fraction division algorithm.
Dividing numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor produces an equivalent fraction in lowest terms.
The least common multiple of the denominators provides a shared unit for combining the fractions.
Equivalent fractions let both quantities be renamed with the same denominator before combining them.
Removing a common factor from numerator and denominator preserves a fraction’s value.
An area model shows why multiplying fractions multiplies both the numerators and the denominators.
Prime factorizations expose the shared prime factors whose product is the greatest common factor.
Using each prime factor with its greatest required exponent constructs a multiple shared by both numbers.
Naming the two compared quantities gives meaning to the order of the numbers in ratio notation.
Multiplying both quantities by the same whole-number factor preserves their ratio.
A ratio table lists pairs generated by scaling both quantities by the same factor.
A unit rate rescales a ratio so the second quantity is one unit.
Dividing the first quantity by the second calculates the amount per one unit.
Speed is the unit rate obtained by dividing distance by elapsed time.
Ratio notation preserves which two quantities are being compared when translating a word problem.
Dividing the fractional quantities calculates the amount corresponding to one unit of the second quantity.
A proportional table maintains equivalent ratios between corresponding nonzero entries.
In a proportional table the unit rate is the constant multiplier from the input to the output.
Recognizing the same multiplier in every row supports writing the relationship as y = kx.
The table’s constant ratio supplies the coefficient k in y = kx.
A percent is a rate per hundred; multiplying that rate by the whole gives the corresponding part.
An increase adds a percentage of the original quantity to that original quantity.
A decrease subtracts a percentage of the original quantity from that original quantity.
A tax amount is the stated percentage of the pretax price.
A percentage tip is found by scaling the bill by the tip rate.
The discount amount is a percentage of the original price and is subtracted to find the sale price.
Absolute value measures the distance of a number from zero on the number line.
Positions farther right on a number line represent greater numbers.
Subtracting an integer can be understood as adding its opposite.
Distance is the absolute value of the difference, ensuring a nonnegative length.
Coefficients count copies of a variable term, so like terms combine by adding their coefficients.
Factoring reverses distribution by identifying a factor common to each term.
Grouping symbols show which quantities stay together when using inverse operations in an equation.
Strict and inclusive inequality symbols determine open or filled boundary points and the shaded direction.
Integer exponent rules define positive, zero, and negative powers consistently.
An exponential expression uses exponents to describe powers.
Multiplying the coefficients and powers of ten separately uses the structure of scientific notation.
Dividing the coefficients and powers of ten separately uses the structure of scientific notation.
Finding a missing side from its squared length requires taking a square root.
Horizontal and vertical coordinate differences form the legs of a right triangle whose hypotenuse is the point-to-point distance.
Writing the Pythagorean calculation in coordinate symbols gives the distance formula.
Slope specifies the vertical change per horizontal unit in the linear equation.
The y-intercept supplies b, the value of y when x is zero.
Graphing both equations allows their shared solution to be read at the intersection.
An intersection gives values that satisfy both equations of a system.
Solving one equation provides the algebra used to find values satisfying a system.
A function is a mapping that assigns exactly one output to each input.
A function assigns an output to an input; evaluating f(x) computes that assigned output.
Slope measures the rate of change of y for each unit increase in x.
A scatter plot displays paired measurements so their direction, form, and strength of association can be described.
A scatter plot shows the paired data whose overall linear trend the fitted line summarizes.
A fitted line provides predicted output values for chosen inputs.
The interquartile range is the upper quartile minus the lower quartile.
Mean absolute deviation averages the absolute distances of the data values from their mean.
A table cell counts observations belonging to both of its row and column categories.
Dividing a cell count by its row or column total describes a proportion within that selected group.
An event is the set of outcomes whose chance a probability describes.
A tree organizes the same possible outcome sequences into successive branches.
Counting unit cubes gives a measure of the space occupied by a solid.
Counting cubes in one layer and multiplying by the number of layers yields length × width × height.
The area formula uses the radius squared, so the radius must be distinguished from the diameter.
The circumference formulas use either the diameter or twice the radius.
Multiplying the circular base area by the height gives the volume of a cylinder.
A cone with the same base and height has one third of the corresponding cylinder’s volume.
